bullets.title: MU: UBS raises PT to $1,625 on DRAM supercycle, memory stocks 17% off peak seen as buying opportunity
bullets.body: UBS upgrades 2H26 DDR contract pricing to +32% QoQ in 3Q26 (from +17% prior) and +18% QoQ in 4Q26; NAND raised to +30% QoQ in 3Q26. DRAM stays undersupplied until at least 2Q28 with 2027 bit demand growth (+36.2% YoY) far exceeding supply (+19.3%); industry revenues forecast $992bn in 2026 and $1.76tn in 2027 generating ~$1.2tn FCF. Micron rated Buy at $1,625 PT; memory stocks down 17% from June peak seen as temporary pullback with main risk being hyperscaler affordability.

bullets.title: TSLA: Q2 deliveries beat consensus by 18%, highest growth rate since 3Q23
bullets.body: Tesla posted record Q2 deliveries led by Europe, beating consensus by 18% per Morgan Stanley — the strongest YoY growth rate since 3Q23. Energy storage came in ahead of MS estimates and in line with consensus, with demand robust from utility-scale ESS and data center customers. Result raises hopes of ending a two-year annual delivery decline.

bullets.title: META: Samsung $6.54B MTIA chip deal; Zuckerberg admits AI agent progress slower than expected
bullets.body: Samsung Foundry is in negotiations for an over KRW10T ($6.54B) contract to mass-produce Meta's third-generation MTIA custom AI chips, with Meta's 'Watermelon' model claimed to have caught up to OpenAI's GPT-5.5. Separately, Zuckerberg acknowledged AI agent development has been slower than expected over the past four months, with company reorganization and major job cuts not yet delivering results; he expects more significant AI benefits within 3-6 months. Tesla is capping employee AI spending at $200/week starting July 6.

bullets.title: NAND/DRAM: Morgan Stanley sees 9% NAND supply shortage in 2027; prefers DRAM tactically
bullets.body: MS projects AI-related NAND demand to increase 60% YoY, creating a 9% supply shortage in 2027 that persists into 2028 when node migration and greenfield expansion provide relief. MS tactically prefers DRAM over NAND due to better LTA terms, higher demand visibility, and supply discipline; NAND suppliers with LTA agreements benefit from downside protection. Complements UBS's bullish DRAM view, with both houses pointing to unprecedented demand/supply gaps.

bullets.title: NVDA: China L2 ADAS mandate (Jan 2027) benefits NVDA/TXN as chip suppliers to consolidating ADAS ecosystem
bullets.body: China's MIIT announced its first mandatory L2 ADAS standard (GB 47955-2026) effective Jan 1, 2027, requiring hands-off steering detection and driver monitoring systems. Policy is expected to eliminate low-ROI ADAS development by smaller automakers, consolidating toward solution providers like Horizon Robotics and Xpeng — with NVIDIA and TXN identified as key chip suppliers benefiting from the shift. L3 ADAS policy is expected later in 2H26 with similar safety-focused norms.

bullets.title: SEI, WULF, VST, CEG, GEV: Power/AI energy plays with near-term catalysts
bullets.body: MS feedback flags SEI in mid-to-high $60s back to value levels with three hyperscaler customers anchoring growth; low $60s represents existing capacity value without growth optionality. WULF awaiting Kentucky site deal with a perceived lower bar; crypto miners see headline reaction as overreaction. ERCOT Batch Zero approved by PUCT with ~35 GW baseload and ~65 GW study demand supporting IPP contracting; NRG has secured 5.4 GW H-class turbines from GEV with Kiewit EPC agreement, a positive read-through for VST and CEG.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY online sports betting 2QTD GGR -12% Y/Y despite World Cup handle boost; hold rates compressed
bullets.body: DraftKings 2QTD NY GGR declined 16% YoY with GGR market share slipping to 33% from 34%; the week ending 6/28 saw +100% YoY GGR on a 12.1% hold rate boosted by World Cup. FanDuel and Fanatics gained share while DraftKings and FanDuel saw share erosion. 2QTD hold rates compressed 200bps YoY to 8.7%, weighing on GGR despite handle growth.

bullets.title: BABA: Alibaba bans Anthropic Claude Code for employees citing security concerns amid escalating dispute
bullets.body: Alibaba is instructing employees to use its internal Qoder platform instead of Claude Code, citing concerns that Claude Code features can identify users with China links as a security risk. The ban widens an existing dispute after Anthropic accused Alibaba of illicitly accessing Claude AI via fake accounts. The confrontation adds a geopolitical dimension to AI tooling competition in China.

bullets.title: SPOT: Spotify disputes Kalshi/Polymarket partnerships after song-ranking manipulation via prediction market bets
bullets.body: Spotify asked Kalshi and Polymarket to remove its logo and clarify that no partnership exists after identifying users manipulating song rankings tied to prediction market bets. This represents a novel platform-integrity risk for Spotify as prediction markets grow in scope and consumer engagement.

bullets.title: RCL, CCL: UBS sees outperformance in 2026 on yield growth; NCLH lags on strategic missteps
bullets.body: UBS projects RCL net yield +1.6% YoY and CCL +1.8% YoY in 2026E, with both names outperforming NCLH which faces net yield declining -4.6% YoY due to strategic missteps where net revenue yield may not grow faster than net cruise cost. Viking (VIK) leads the group at +5.8% net yield growth. Top 3 cruise lines control ~90% of the North American market.

bullets.title: Mag 7 / Software: Strong hedge fund selling in June; AI momentum rolling over from June 22 peak
bullets.body: JPM prime services notes strong selling of Mag 7 and Software (both at -2 Z-score) in recent flows, with US Momentum down 17% from its June 22 peak. Asia fundamental L/S funds posted strong June returns (+7.1%) but Info Tech/Semis dominated selling flows at record pace, reversing all May buying. AI Tech Beneficiaries index (MSXXAIB) posted its largest day of active net reduction with Broad AI L/S ratio near a 5-year low — a positioning warning for the group.

bullets.title: MSFT: Merging Copilot consumer and business apps; launching $2.5B Microsoft Frontier Company for AI integration
bullets.body: Microsoft will merge its Copilot consumer and business apps into a single product to compete directly with ChatGPT and Claude. Additionally, Microsoft is launching Microsoft Frontier Company with $2.5bn in capital to help customers integrate multiple AI technologies. Separately, Chevron's 20-year contract with Microsoft provides a supportive datapoint for AI-power infrastructure contracting.

bullets.title: MU: Citi highlights SK Hynix removing price caps from LTAs; memory semi-customization trend accelerating
bullets.body: SK Hynix is adopting long-term supply agreements without industry-standard price caps, allowing spot market increases to flow through during shortages — a structurally bullish pricing dynamic. Hynix and Samsung are extending contract durations to 3-5 years; Micron is setting price caps at 2Q26 levels with price floors. The memory market is shifting toward semi-customization driven by diversified AI product demand, benefiting suppliers with flexible contract structures.

bullets.title: AMZN: Deployed enough LEO satellites to launch service competing with Starlink later this year
bullets.body: Amazon has deployed sufficient satellites to launch its Project Kuiper LEO broadband service later in 2026, putting it in direct competition with SpaceX's Starlink. No specific financial targets were cited but the milestone represents a meaningful commercial catalyst for Amazon's broadband ambitions.

bullets.title: Macro: Wolfe forecasts June core CPI at 0.23% vs 0.3% consensus; Fed likely on hold through summer
bullets.body: Wolfe Research forecasts June core CPI at 0.23% MoM vs the 0.3% consensus, with headline CPI at -0.06% MoM driven by lower energy prices following the end of the Iran conflict. World Cup is expected to add 3-4bp temporary boost through lodging; core PCE seen at 0.27% MoM with YoY run rate at 3.4%. Softer labor data (June payrolls +57k) should keep the Fed comfortable on hold over summer, though JPM's longer-run view is for higher rates as labor supply tightens unemployment toward 4%.
